verdict.rationale: Codex documents a sandbox for command execution, with rules governing which commands may run outside it. That implies tests and commands run in an isolated sandbox rather than as a dry-run, but the evidence is a single passing mention. Nothing describes how the sandbox is scoped, what it isolates, or how it keeps production data out of reach. missing for 10: documentation of sandbox isolation scope (filesystem/network boundaries), explicit separation from production data or credentials, a dedicated test or staging environment, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use rules to control which commands Codex can run outside the sandbox.
Debug code, run tests, review a PR, implement a feature
